description:
Gate-run records are stored and read by key, so reading one issue's runs, its latest run of a gate, or a reusable verdict never reads another key's records.

## Background

Gate runs were stored flat, and every reader enumerated and parsed all of them. This story stores runs per issue, names each issue's latest run of a gate on its gate state, finds reusable verdicts through a per-key verdict record, captures only the evaluated issue's latest runs into gate mutations, and rewrites this repository's recorded runs once into that layout.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Reading one issue's latest runs or its run history opens only that issue's run records.
- [hard] REQ-02: Reuse reads one verdict record and the run it names.
- [hard] REQ-03: Gate evaluation, precheck planning and validation capture no other issue's run records.
- [hard] REQ-04: This repository's recorded runs, latest-run references and verdict records are in the per-key layout, and every cited run id resolves.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Gate runs are addressed per issue, per gate and per inputs digest
